\]

We view the grid as a graph with \(64\) vertices and \(112\) edges (horizontal and vertical adjacencies).

For a set \(S\) of cells, let \(\partial S\) be the number of edges with one endpoint in \(S\) and one endpoint outside \(S\).

If the cells with labels at most \(t\) are \(S_t\), then an edge whose labels are \(p<q\) is counted in \(\partial S_t\) exactly for \(t=p,p+1,\dots,q-1\), i.e. exactly \(q-p\) times. Hence

\[
M=\sum_{t=1}^{63} \partial S_t.
\]

So we need upper bounds for the largest possible boundary of a set of \(k\) cells.

---

## 1. Maximum boundary of \(k\) cells

Let \(F(k)\) be the maximum possible value of \(\partial S\) over all sets \(S\) of \(k\) cells. By taking complements,

\[
F(k)=F(64-k),
\]

so it suffices to understand \(1\le k\le 32\).

The total number of edges in the \(8\times 8\) grid is

\[
8\cdot 7+8\cdot 7=112.
\]

We will show:

\[
F(k)=
\begin{cases}
4k, & 1\le k\le 18,\\[2mm]
3k+18, & 19\le k\le 30,\\[2mm]
110, & k=31,\\[2mm]
112, & k=32.
\end{cases}
\]

---

### Case 1: \(1\le k\le 18\)

Every cell has degree at most \(4\), so

\[
\partial S\le \sum_{v\in S}\deg(v)\le 4k.
\]

This is attainable by choosing \(k\) mutually nonadjacent interior cells of the same checkerboard color. There are \(18\) such cells.

Thus \(F(k)=4k\) for \(1\le k\le 18\).

---

### Case 2: \(19\le k\le 30\)

Let \(S\) have \(k\) cells. Let

- \(m\) be the number of selected cells in the \(6\times 6\) interior,
- \(e\) be the number of adjacent pairs fully inside \(S\),
- \(x\) be the number of selected non-corner boundary cells,
- \(y\) be the number of selected corner cells.

The sum of the degrees of the selected cells is

\[
4k-x-2y.
\]

Each internal adjacent pair subtracts \(2\) from the boundary count, so

\[
\partial S=4k-x-2y-2e.
\]

We need a lower bound on the “loss”

\[
L=x+2y+2e.
\]

Pair the \(36\) interior cells into \(18\) disjoint adjacent pairs. If \(m\le 18\), then

\[
L\ge x+y=k-m\ge k-18.
\]

If \(m\ge 19\), then by the pigeonhole principle at least \(m-18\) of those interior pairs are fully selected, so \(e\ge m-18\). Also \(x+y=k-m\), so

\[
L\ge (k-m)+2(m-18)=k+m-36\ge k-18.
\]

Therefore in all cases,

\[
L\ge k-18,
\]

and hence

\[
\partial S\le 4k-(k-18)=3k+18.
\]

This bound is attainable by taking all \(18\) interior cells of one checkerboard color and \(k-18\) non-corner boundary cells of that same color. Those cells are mutually nonadjacent, and their degrees are \(4\) and \(3\), respectively.

Thus \(F(k)=3k+18\) for \(19\le k\le 30\).

---

### Case 3: \(k=31,32\)

Clearly \(F(32)\le 112\), and equality is achieved by taking one entire checkerboard color class. Thus

\[
F(32)=112.
\]

For \(k=31\), we prove \(F(31)\le 110\). Let \(S\) have \(31\) cells and let \(T\) be its complement, so \(|T|=33\).

We need the fact that the only independent sets of size \(32\) in an \(8\times 8\) grid are the two checkerboard color classes.

Indeed, an independent set can contain at most one cell from each of the \(32\) horizontal dominoes, so its size is at most \(32\). If it has size \(32\), then each row must contain exactly \(4\) selected cells. In consecutive rows, the selected columns must be disjoint, so the second row must select exactly the complement of the first row’s columns. Since both rows are independent, the first row’s selected and unselected columns both avoid adjacent columns, forcing an alternating pattern. Thus the whole set is one of the two checkerboard color classes.

Now since \(|T|=33>32\), \(T\) cannot be independent, so it contains at least one internal edge. If \(S\) also contains an internal edge, then together they account for at least two edges not crossing the cut, giving

\[
\partial S\le 112-2=110.
\]

If \(S\) is independent but \(T\) has exactly one internal edge, removing one endpoint of that edge from \(T\) leaves an independent set of size \(32\), hence a full checkerboard color class. The removed vertex has degree at least \(2\), and all of its neighbors lie in that color class, so it would actually create at least two internal edges, contradiction. Therefore \(T\) has at least two internal edges, and again

\[
\partial S\le 110.
\]

Equality is achieved by taking one checkerboard color class and deleting a corner cell, whose degree is \(2\). Thus

\[
F(31)=110.
\]

---

## 2. Upper bound for \(M\)

We now sum the maximum possible boundary sizes.

For \(1\le k\le 32\),

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{32} F(k)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{18}4k
+
\sum_{k=19}^{30}(3k+18)
+
110+112.
\]

Compute:

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{18}4k=4\cdot \frac{18\cdot 19}{2}=4\cdot 171=684.
\]

\[
\sum_{k=19}^{30}(3k+18)
=
3\sum_{k=19}^{30}k+18\cdot 12.
\]

There are \(12\) terms, and

\[
\sum_{k=19}^{30}k=\frac{12(19+30)}2=294,
\]

so this part is

\[
3\cdot 294+216=882+216=1098.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{32}F(k)=684+1098+110+112=2004.
\]

Using symmetry \(F(k)=F(64-k)\),

\[
\sum_{t=1}^{63}F(t)=2\cdot 2004-112=3896.
\]

Therefore

\[
M\le 3896.
\]

---

## 3. Construction attaining \(3896\)

Color the board like a chessboard. Put labels \(1\) through \(32\) on the black cells and \(33\) through \(64\) on the white cells as follows:

- Black interior cells: labels \(1\) to \(18\).
- Black non-corner boundary cells: labels \(19\) to \(30\).
- Black corners: labels \(31,32\).
- White corners: labels \(33,34\).
- White non-corner boundary cells: labels \(35\) to \(46\).
- White interior cells: labels \(47\) to \(64\).

Every edge joins a black cell to a white cell, and every white label is larger than every black label. Therefore

\[
M=\sum_{\text{white }w}\deg(w)\cdot \text{label}(w)
-
\sum_{\text{black }b}\deg(b)\cdot \text{label}(b).
\]

Each color class has \(18\) interior cells, \(12\) non-corner boundary cells, and \(2\) corners.

For black cells:

\[
4(1+\cdots+18)+3(19+\cdots+30)+2(31+32)
\]

\[
=4\cdot 171+3\cdot 294+2\cdot 63
=684+882+126=1692.
\]

For white cells:

\[
2(33+34)+3(35+\cdots+46)+4(47+\cdots+64)
\]

\[
=2\cdot 67+3\cdot 486+4\cdot 999
=134+1458+3996=5588.
\]

Thus

\[
M=5588-1692=3896.
\]

So the maximum possible value of \(M\) is \(3896\). The remainder when divided by \(1000\) is

\[
3896\equiv 896\pmod{1000}.
\]

\[
\boxed{896}
